---
title: "Does the reconstructed airframe reproduce published wing loading and static margin?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0
PROBE_POOL = 200.0
PROBE_SPENT = 8.9

# Published reference values
S_pub = 115 * 0.0254**2
wl_pub = (MASS_AUW * 1e3) / (S_pub * 1e2)

# Reconstructed geometry and wing loading
S_recon = airplane.s_ref
wl_recon = (MASS_AUW * 1e3) / (S_recon * 1e2)
wl_delta_pct = (wl_recon - wl_pub) / wl_pub * 100

# Level flight trim and stability at alpha = 2 deg
v_trim = find_trim_speed(airplane, mass=MASS_AUW, alpha=2.0)
trim_stab = evaluate_stability(airplane, velocity=v_trim, alpha=2.0)
sm_trim = trim_stab["static_margin"]
x_np_trim = trim_stab["x_np"]
cg_pct_mac = (airplane.xyz_ref[0] - wing.xsecs[0].xyz_le[0]) / airplane.c_ref * 100
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{sm_trim * 100:.1f}% MAC"`]{.hero-value}
[Static margin at published 25 mm CG in cruise trim]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** No. Reconstructing the airframe gives a wing area of [`{python} f"{S_recon*1e2:.2f} dm²"`]{.key}, yielding [`{python} f"{wl_recon:.1f} g/dm²"`]{.key} wing loading at [`{python} f"{MASS_AUW*1e3:.0f} g"`]{.key} all-up weight. This is [`{python} f"{wl_delta_pct:+.1f}%"`]{.key} higher than the published [`{python} f"{wl_pub:.1f} g/dm²"`]{.key}, which assumed nominal [`{python} f"{S_pub*1e2:.2f} dm²"`]{.key} area. At the published [`{python} f"{CG_X*1e3:.0f} mm"`]{.key} CG ([`{python} f"{cg_pct_mac:.1f}%"`]{.key} MAC), the neutral point at cruise trim ([`{python} f"{v_trim:.1f} m/s"`]{.key}) sits at [`{python} f"{x_np_trim*1e3:.1f} mm"`]{.key}. This yields a heavy static margin of [`{python} f"{sm_trim*100:.1f}%"`]{.key} MAC (@fig-three-view).
